controls.reason: Configured monitors for inventoried properties do not prove complete property coverage or that all eight signal classes are actually detected and delivered.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed sites can have enabled monitors while a locale host is omitted or the manual-action query is broken. Configuration passes although required monitoring is absent.

controls.reason: A classification schema and counts do not prove that server events are correctly distinguished among discovery, fetch, rendering, redirect, rate-limit, and failure causes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rendering-resource failure can be mislabeled fetch while every category has counts and source events. The report passes shape checks but does not distinguish the actual problem.

controls.reason: Grouped reports assume complete intended URL and search-engine inventories, while external indexed counts may be sampled or incomplete.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed host and locale can report matching counts while an omitted template is largely deindexed. All groups pass but intended versus actual indexing is not fully monitored.

controls.reason: Event ledgers can omit changes, and deciding which dashboards are relevant requires contextual judgment not supplied by annotation identity matching.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All recorded incidents can be annotated on one declared dashboard while an unrecorded template migration affects another dashboard. The clause passes but relevant annotations are missing.

controls.reason: Active alert definitions do not prove that queries, thresholds, and notification delivery detect sudden harmful changes for each signal.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every alert can be enabled with a threshold that never fires or a broken destination. Coverage fields pass while sudden accessibility or canonical failures produce no alert.

controls.reason: Critical-page and error-state inventories are not complete, and selected route fixtures cannot prove correct status behavior across all authorization and failure paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed pages can return 404 in fixtures while an omitted account page returns 200 with Not found for another tenant. Tests pass but a critical page still gives misleading success.

controls.reason: A non-automation evidence link does not prove a valid WCAG conformance basis; manual scope and conformance judgment require accessibility expertise.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A claim can link to a one-page manual checklist in addition to an overlay. Record validation passes although the evidence is nowhere near sufficient for WCAG conformance.

controls.reason: Field retention does not prove valid applicability, complete scope and assumptions, or accountable owners, reviewers, and decision authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A package can retain placeholder scope, nominal owners, and an unauthorized reviewer with valid dates. All fields exist while the governance record is not substantively valid.

controls.reason: Exact source-revision identifiers and immutable verification records make revision binding a complete objective property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A result from another or modified revision cannot pass the equality and integrity checks; missing bindings fail or block.

controls.reason: Severity, impact, compensating-control adequacy, and accountable ownership require judgment; required fields alone do not prove correct retained risk records.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical defect can be labeled low, link an irrelevant monitor, and name an inactive owner while all fields pass. The unresolved risk is misrepresented.

controls.reason: One current postdeployment result does not prove that a continuous control continues to operate throughout relevant time and conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A daily control can emit one success after deployment and then stop permanently. Its timestamp passes while ongoing control operation is not evidenced.

controls.reason: The change ledger cannot prove every post-snapshot change was captured, and mapping affected controls requires semantic impact judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded commit can map to reassessed controls while an unlogged production flag change is omitted. The clause passes although affected evidence was not reassessed.

controls.reason: A deployed-verification record does not prove that its protocol verifies the outcome claimed by a tool, supplier, certification, or policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A supplier security claim can link to a production health check. The record is current and bound but does not verify the claimed security outcome.

controls.reason: The surface inventory may omit routes, and selecting applicable public, searchable, shareable, private, or removed states requires product judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed pages can have visibility labels while an unlisted export is publicly reachable, or a private page is mislabeled public. The schema passes but intended surfaces are not identified.

controls.reason: Exact-one directory identities do not prove accepted accountable ownership for the seven accessibility, content, and discovery domains.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Inactive or nominal users can be assigned and resolve successfully while nobody exercises ownership. Cardinality passes without accountability.

controls.reason: The seven success domains each require a metric, operator, threshold, and window, making definition and measurability objectively checkable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing or unevaluable criteria fail; whether chosen targets are ambitious is outside this definition-only control.

controls.reason: Six documentation sections do not prove accurate effects on accessibility and search for every personalized state and experiment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each section can say no effect while geolocation hides content from crawlers and consent changes keyboard order. Presence passes but behavior is undocumented truthfully.

controls.reason: Linked criteria can be irrelevant, and deciding applicability and adequate accessibility or discoverability acceptance criteria requires semantic review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every requirement can link to a generic alt text exists check while a dynamic search feature lacks indexability criteria. Links pass but acceptance coverage is missing.

controls.reason: Naming a methodology and populating scope and sample fields does not prove representative sampling or correct methodology application.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A plan can call one homepage representative of a thousand templates and pass every field. The evaluation methodology is named but not validly applied.

controls.reason: A supported setting matrix and assertions cannot exhaust content states, and readability or loss of function requires accessibility and user judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Fixtures can pass at one viewport while a localized modal becomes unreadable at 400 percent zoom. All approved cases pass but supported content still fails.

controls.reason: Evidence labels for five modalities do not establish expert quality, representative users, adequate scope, or a valid conformance conclusion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A trivial automated scan plus one-minute manual and user records can satisfy modality presence while critical keyboard journeys remain untested.

controls.reason: The rule is limited to recording an exact finite metadata set with versioned references, making completeness and referential integrity bounded.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing standards, tools, platform, sample, or limitation fields fail; evaluation adequacy is judged separately.

controls.reason: Authoritative source references expose normative status, and the three provenance labels form an exact classification enum.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A heuristic labeled normative conflicts with its source and fails; correctly referenced status passes deterministically.

controls.reason: The scoring gate has a precise invariant that any inaccessible critical journey forces failure regardless of low-value page pass counts.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A configuration that averages away one critical failure fails static policy evaluation; compliant decision logic passes.

controls.reason: Declared asynchronous-state fixtures do not enumerate every update path or prove messages are useful and timely for assistive technology.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A loading fixture can announce correctly while a background save failure updates silently. All listed states pass but an asynchronous update remains inaccessible.

controls.reason: Accessibility-tree equality to declared snapshots does not prove that semantic order and relationships remain meaningful to users through every transformation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A virtualized table can match a flawed expected snapshot while screen-reader reading order is confusing. Fixtures pass but semantics are not preserved.

controls.reason: The approved action inventory can omit controls, and selected keyboard paths do not prove operability across state, role, locale, and error conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed button can work by keyboard while an unlisted drag handle or error-state control still needs a pointer. The suite passes but not every actionable function is operable.

controls.reason: Finite tab and escape tests cannot prove that no keyboard-only sequence becomes trapped across dynamic focus states and nested interactions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dialog exits in the fixture but traps focus after a validation error or nested popup. All documented exits pass while another reachable keyboard sequence remains trapped.

controls.reason: Contrast and area are measurable, but clearly visible and complete focus-state coverage require visual judgment and a complete element-state inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every tested default control can meet thresholds while a focus ring is obscured on a patterned background or missing in an unlisted state. Numeric fixtures pass but focus is not clearly visible.

controls.reason: A viewport matrix cannot exhaust overlay, keyboard, zoom, locale, and dynamic layout combinations that may obscure focused elements.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All standard viewports can pass while a translated banner plus virtual keyboard covers the submit button. The matrix passes but focused content is hidden in a supported combination.

controls.reason: Identifying repeated blocks and whether alternative navigation is equivalent requires page-structure and user-flow judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A page can declare no repeated block or provide a skip link to the wrong landmark. The fixture passes its declared destination while repeated navigation remains burdensome.

controls.reason: Shortcut safety depends on assistive technology, browser, locale, focus, and platform combinations not bounded by a few collision tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A shortcut can remap in the tested screen reader but conflict in another supported voice or keyboard layout. All fixtures pass while a single-character conflict remains.

controls.reason: The drag-action inventory may omit interactions, and same declared outcome does not prove functional equivalence across data and state paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A card reorder fixture has buttons while an unlisted map drag has no alternative, or the button loses metadata. Tests pass but drag functionality is not fully accessible.

controls.reason: Complex-gesture inventories and declared outcomes can omit gestures or meaningful side effects, so selected alternatives do not prove universal equivalence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Pinch zoom can have buttons in fixtures while a path gesture is unlisted, or the alternative skips precision state. The suite passes though a complex gesture lacks an equivalent.

controls.reason: Which actions need cancellation or reversal is a consequence judgment, so testing only actions marked cancellation-required can omit harmful pointer-down behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A destructive selection can be mislabeled cancellation-not-required and commit on pointer-down. Every marked action passes while the original safety rule is violated.

controls.reason: Consequential-action classification and an approved undo path require judgment, while fixtures cannot prove reversal under all side effects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A charge action can be omitted from the consequential list or its undo reverse UI state but not payment. Tests pass while consequential effects cannot truly be undone.

controls.reason: Voice activation varies by engine, locale, pronunciation, hidden accessible names, and control state beyond a finite declared fixture set.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Visible text can activate in one English engine while a supported locale or duplicate label activates the wrong control. Every listed test passes but voice use still fails.

controls.reason: Numeric contrast is bounded for known pixels, but identifying meaningful visuals and every responsive, interactive, theme, and data state requires specialist judgment and complete inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Default icons can meet thresholds while an unlisted chart series or hover state does not. Tested colors pass but meaningful information still lacks required contrast.

controls.reason: Presence and reachability assertions do not fully decide readability or loss of meaning across text, language, viewport, and user settings.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared English content can remain present at 200 percent while localized labels overlap and become unreadable. Fixtures pass but readability is lost.

controls.reason: Which preferences are available and what it means to honor each preference require platform and accessibility interpretation across incomplete combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Reduced motion can be honored in one page while an unlisted canvas ignores it, or high contrast response is technically changed but unusable. Declared tests pass without honoring every setting.

controls.reason: No tested sequence exceeds a threshold is weaker than no reachable visual pattern exceeds it; dynamic frames and generated content are not completely inventoried.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Bundled videos can pass frame analysis while an experiment generates a flashing animation at runtime. All tested sequences pass but the product can exceed seizure thresholds.

controls.reason: Immediately reachable is not given a time or interaction bound, and autoplay paths can vary by browser and user state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A stop control can appear after ten seconds and be called immediate, while tests on one browser pass. Users still receive uncontrolled autoplay audio.

controls.reason: Caption-track presence and synchronization do not prove the captions are accurate, complete, and meaningful for prerecorded or live content.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A perfectly synchronized track can contain unrelated words. Timing tests pass while required captions do not communicate the audio.

controls.reason: Keyboard events and accessibility-tree fields are partial; visible and usable media controls require visual and assistive-technology evaluation across states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Controls can have roles and accept Enter while focus is invisible or a screen reader cannot operate the timeline. Assertions pass but controls are not usable.

controls.reason: Programmatic or pixel visibility assertions do not fully decide perceivability of controls, errors, selection, and state in high-contrast combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All elements can occupy visible pixels while selected and unselected states render identically to a user. Fixtures pass but state is not perceivable.

controls.reason: Distracting classification and effective user control require human judgment, so testing only marked media can omit genuinely distracting content.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rapidly moving carousel can be marked not distracting and have no pause control. Every marked item passes while users cannot control the distraction.

controls.reason: Form schema and rendered pre-submission content form finite field inventories, permitting exact comparison of required state, formats, constraints, and examples.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A field missing any declared instruction before submission fails; complete matching content passes without judging copy style.

controls.reason: Form-field identities and accessibility-tree relationships make error association and multi-error summary linkage exact bounded properties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unassociated error, missing summary, or broken link to any failed field cannot pass the generated invalid-input matrix.

controls.reason: Selected recoverable errors and repeat attempts do not exhaust concurrency, retry, timeout, and side-effect paths needed to prove preservation and duplicate prevention.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A form can preserve input on validation errors and deduplicate sequential clicks while two concurrent retries create duplicate payments. Fixtures pass but duplicate submission remains possible.

controls.reason: A successful alternative in declared journeys does not prove every user can authenticate without the prohibited cognitive task across recovery and risk states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The happy path can use a password manager while suspicious-login recovery requires distorted CAPTCHA transcription. All listed journeys pass but authentication still depends solely on a cognitive task in a reachable state.

controls.reason: Successful fixtures do not establish that multifactor and recovery methods are accessible to users with different disabilities and supported assistive technology.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One password manager and SMS flow can complete while the only recovery option is unusable by screen reader. Scenarios pass but accessible recovery is absent.

controls.reason: Barrier inventories can omit inaccessible states, and determining that an alternative is accessible and equivalent requires specialist and user evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A CAPTCHA flow can list an audio alternative that is unintelligible, or a device-loss path is omitted. Execution succeeds in fixtures while no accessible alternative exists for affected users.

controls.reason: A fixed error suite across four modes cannot exhaust form, account, network, and state errors or assistive-technology combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All declared invalid-field cases can recover while session-expiry recovery loses focus in a supported screen reader. The suite passes but error recovery remains broken.

controls.reason: Supported geometry matrices cannot exhaust keyboard types, cutouts, zoom levels, orientation, language, banners, and dynamic content combinations.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Standard devices can pass while a localized instruction is covered by a floating keyboard on a supported phone. Fixtures pass but controls are obscured.

controls.reason: A bound suite can miss offline-specific interaction and content states, and accessibility cannot be reduced to selected automated assertions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Cached pages can pass scans while offline error recovery traps keyboard focus. Every declared mode has a green suite but accessibility is not preserved.

controls.reason: Structural equality cannot prove correct reading order, alternate-text meaning, table interpretation, or link purpose after conversion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A converted PDF can retain tags and alternate-text fields while the reading order is illogical and alt text wrong. Assertions pass but semantics are not preserved.

controls.reason: The upgrade ledger and regression suite may omit relevant changes, assistive technologies, components, and behavioral states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded browser upgrade can pass the suite while an unrecorded PDF generator update breaks a supported screen reader. Both clauses pass but compatibility regressed.

controls.reason: Declared API values can be internally consistent yet semantically wrong, and user-agent surface inventories may omit reachable content and states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tree can expose a control as a button with the wrong name and order while matching a flawed declaration. Tests pass but useful accessibility information is not exposed.

controls.reason: Expected snapshots can encode incorrect semantics, and transformation cases cannot exhaust reader, translation, annotation, and export behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A translated export can match a declared tree while headings lose their meaning and reading order. Snapshot equality passes but semantics were flattened.

controls.reason: The interaction matrix cannot exhaust browser platform, extension, permission, download, history, setting, and alternative-input states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Keyboard tests can pass in default chrome while a permission dialog or extension state traps focus. Approved cases pass but browser functions remain inaccessible.

controls.reason: Detected regression identities and product-defect record types are exact workflow facts, so every known regression can be required to have the mandated issue type.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A detected regression with no defect or a non-product classification fails; unchanged content does not alter the result.

controls.reason: Which accessibility information is required depends on content semantics, so testing only metadata marked required can omit real omissions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An informative image can be misclassified decorative, preventing an alt-text prompt, while all declared missing fields trigger correctly. Fixtures pass but authors are not prompted for required information.

controls.reason: Requirement and test links do not prove that component contracts contain correct accessibility behavior or that tests verify it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every component can link a generic accessibility note to a lint test. Graph checks pass while keyboard and semantic requirements are absent.

controls.reason: Documentation fields do not prove complete or correct keyboard behavior, semantics, states, constraints, and limitations for each shared component.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A component can fill every field with standard behavior and omit a known focus limitation. The schema passes but consumers lack required documentation.

controls.reason: Individual token thresholds do not prove all token combinations remain accessible, and reviewed exceptions require accountable human judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each color token can pass alone while two allowed tokens combine with insufficient contrast, or an unauthorized reviewer signs an exception. Both clauses pass but inaccessible tokens remain possible.

controls.reason: Whether a behavior change is breaking requires semantic judgment, and declared-change records can omit changes or communication recipients.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An accessibility-name change can be mislabeled nonbreaking and receive no notice while every declared break has email evidence. The clause passes but consumers were not informed.

controls.reason: The supplier register can avoid marking inaccessible components, and a linked plan can be a placeholder with no feasible replacement or isolation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An inaccessible date picker can be marked acceptable, or its plan say replace someday. Record checks pass while no real mitigation plan exists.

controls.reason: Task-evidence presence and score inputs do not prove that procurement evaluated representative tasks or interpreted accessibility correctly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A vendor can receive a task score from opening its login page while critical authoring flows are inaccessible. The formula uses task evidence but not actual product accessibility.

controls.reason: Declared repeatable defect classes and artifact inventories can omit detectable rules, components, documents, and critical flows.
controls.counterexample_analysis: CI can run checks for listed templates while an unlisted PDF generator has repeatable heading defects. Coverage passes but automatable defects remain unchecked.

controls.reason: Metadata and false-positive or false-negative fields do not prove automation is only a floor or that error rates and rule coverage are measured completely.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Runs can record zero false negatives without a discovery protocol and be used as conformance proof. All fields pass while automation governance violates the rule.

controls.reason: One current script per named area does not prove scripts cover meaningful journeys, platforms, states, and expected outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The keyboard script can test only Tab on the homepage and the cognitive script can be empty boilerplate. Library coverage passes while manual testing is inadequate.

controls.reason: Feedback-form schema and submission validation can directly prove that diagnosis disclosure is neither present nor required.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A required diagnosis field or diagnosis-dependent validation fails; successful diagnosis-free submission passes.

controls.reason: The exposing input-mode or assistive-technology identity and retest environment are exact defect-record bindings, making same-mode successful retest objectively checkable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A fix tested only with another mode, with no original mode identity, or with a failing retest cannot pass.

controls.reason: Backlog fields do not prove accountable ownership, correct impact and affected surfaces, useful workaround, or valid closure evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A critical screen-reader defect can be labeled minor, name an inactive owner, and close against an unrelated screenshot. The record passes but the backlog is not truthful.

controls.reason: Monitored supplier changes and a bound suite do not prove complete third-party inventory, change detection, or adequate accessibility regression coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An embedded widget can update outside the monitored version feed, or the suite checks only contrast. Recorded changes pass while a supplier regression reaches users.

controls.reason: Recorded diffs can omit real scope or limitation changes, and a review record does not prove a valid specialist review.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All logged changes can link to signed reviews while a known new limitation is never recorded. The clause passes although statements remain stale.

controls.reason: Exact-one identities do not prove accepted accountable ownership for technical SEO, editorial, international, migration, or monitoring duties.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Nominal or inactive accounts can fill every domain and resolve successfully while no one owns the work.

controls.reason: Which engines, regional services, vertical products, and crawlers matter is a product and market judgment that a list cannot validate.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The record can omit a regional engine used by customers and still be structurally complete. It documents a list, but not the services that actually matter.

controls.reason: Five policy sections do not prove lawful licensing, training, archival, and retrieval decisions or usable crawler rules.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Each heading can contain allow as text while contracts prohibit training use. Presence passes but the crawler policy is substantively wrong.

controls.reason: Documentation distinction is bounded, but the confidential-asset inventory and access probes cannot prove no asset relies only on crawler compliance.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed secret page can require login while an unlisted private PDF is protected only by robots.txt. Both clauses pass but confidentiality still relies on crawler behavior.

controls.reason: An intended-public URL inventory cannot prove completeness, and graph reachability in one crawl does not guarantee stable discovery across variants and dynamic states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed pages can be reachable while an omitted locale page has no link, or a temporary experiment link disappears. The graph passes but not every intended page is stably discoverable.

controls.reason: Private-page classifications can omit or misclassify resources, and one unauthenticated probe does not cover alternate hosts, methods, caches, and object URLs.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed private page can reject GET while an unlisted export or HEAD/object-store URL remains public. Tests pass but a page that must remain private is exposed.

controls.reason: RFC parsing is deterministic, but the universal confidentiality claim depends on a complete asset and access-path inventory not established by tests.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All robots files can conform and listed confidential pages require auth while an omitted document relies only on Disallow. Both clauses pass but robots.txt substitutes for protection.

controls.reason: Relevant host and protocol inventories are assumed complete, and configured monitors do not prove every live robots file is reachable and consistent.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed HTTPS hosts can pass while an HTTP, regional, or legacy host serves a different invalid robots file. Both clauses pass but consistency is incomplete.

controls.reason: Public-but-nonindexable resource and crawler inventories can omit URLs or variants, so passing retrieval tests do not prove universal directive exposure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every listed URL can return noindex to one crawler while an unlisted parameter variant or locale lacks it. Tests pass but public nonindexable content can be indexed.

controls.reason: Declared intent determines the required mechanism and can be wrong or incomplete; the resource inventory can also omit robots-only protections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A confidential download can be mislabeled crawl-only and use Disallow, or remain outside the inventory. Every declared intent passes while robots.txt still substitutes for authentication.

controls.reason: Deleted URL and internal-link inventories cannot prove that every deletion and dynamically generated link is included.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed deletions can return correct status and disappear from crawled links while an omitted locale URL remains 200 and linked from a script. Both clauses pass but deleted content remains.

controls.reason: Which maintenance is short and which routes are affected are not objectively complete, so declared-state probes can omit misleading success pages.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Listed API routes can return 503 while an omitted critical page returns 200 with maintenance text. Tests pass but short maintenance still uses misleading success.

controls.reason: Declared error fixtures cannot enumerate every missing identifier, authorization state, dependency failure, and dynamically rendered error body.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known cases can return 404 while an untested malformed ID returns 200 with an error message. The suite passes but a soft error remains.

controls.reason: Route families and a bounded crawl limit cannot prove absence of inputs that trigger larger or cyclic URL expansion beyond the tested frontier.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A calendar passes a 10,000-URL simulation while one date parameter creates infinite future pages after that bound. Both clauses pass but a crawl trap exists.

controls.reason: Private media inventories and public probes cannot prove coverage of every CDN alias, signed-link state, cache, method, and document asset.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed private files can reject unauthenticated GET while an omitted CDN alias exposes the same bytes. Tests pass but private media remains public.

controls.reason: Current public tests for declared controls do not prove that every deployed crawl and indexing control was identified or tested with complete outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered directives can have a result while an unlisted canonical rule or locale header is untested. The clause passes but production controls are not fully tested.

controls.reason: Declared canonical and locale intent can be incomplete or wrong, and the URL inventory cannot prove coverage of every rendered and generated representation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed URLs can align while an omitted parameter page points to the wrong locale canonical, or the intended target itself is mistaken. Checks pass but declarations remain misaligned.
